question: Dnes vás po splave Váhu odvezie autobus aj s loďou. Prečo sa však starí pltníci z Liptova nemuseli so svojou plťou nijako vracať proti prúdu?
source_excerpt: pltníci plavili drevo z Pienin až do Baltického mora

extra.why_interesting: Anyone who has paddled the Váh knows the hard part is getting the boat back upstream. The twist is that the old raftsmen didn't need to: the raft itself was the cargo. A player can reason this out ('what was the raft made of?'), which gives a satisfying 'I worked it out' moment.
extra.verification_notes: No source contradicts it; the historical practice was that the raft was timber cargo sold at the destination, though I found no page stating this explicitly (searched teraz.sk and sita.sk coverage of Slovak rafting).

explanation: Plť bola zároveň tovarom. Pltníci ju v cieli rozobrali, kmene predali a domov sa vrátili pešo.

question: Keď sa v lete spúšťate na kanoe po Hrone, plávate po rieke, ktorú pred vyše 1800 rokmi spomenul rímsky cisár. Pri jej brehoch vraj písal svoje slávne filozofické Hovory k sebe. Ktorý cisár to bol?
source_excerpt: Written on the Granua (Hron), among the Quadi

extra.why_interesting: Paddlers think of the Hron as a relaxed local summer river. It is a surprise that a world-famous Roman emperor-philosopher named it in one of the best-known books of antiquity. Many players know the emperor from the film Gladiator, so the answer is within reach.
extra.verification_notes: The Meditations colophon says it was written 'among the Quadi on the Granua' (Hron), so Marcus Aurelius is correct; the date is about 1,850 years ago. I did not run a web search to confirm this, so no URL was checked.

explanation: Na konci prvej knihy Hovorov k sebe stojí poznámka „napísané medzi Kvádmi pri Granue“, a Granua je dnešný Hron. Tento cisár je zároveň ten múdry starý vládca z filmu Gladiátor.
